objective_pt: Start and sustain a conversation with a stranger at a professional event: break the ice, describe what you do concisely, find common ground and follow up ("It'd be great to stay in touch").

teacher.goal_pt: Find out how comfortable the learner is approaching strangers in English.
prompts: You're at a conference coffee break. How do you start talking to someone?
How would you describe your job in two sentences?
watchFor: "I work with marketing" (from "trabalho com"); it's "I work in marketing".
Listing job duties instead of the impact of the work.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat in a friendly, open tone.
exercises.prompt: Mind if I join you? I don't think we've met.
accepted: Mind if I join you? I don't think we've met
Do you mind if I join you? I don't think we've met

exercises.instruction_pt: Which is the most natural icebreaker at a conference?
options: Hello. What is your salary?
So, what brings you here today?
I am Carlos. I am engineer.
exercises.explanation_pt: "What brings you here?" is open and friendly. Also note: "I'm an engineer" needs the article "an".

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu trabalho com marketing digital."
accepted: I work in digital marketing
I'm in digital marketing
I work in the digital marketing field

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For your field or industry, use "work in": "I work in digital marketing". "Work with" is for people or tools.
commonErrors.correction_en: I work in digital marketing.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Adjective before the noun: "digital marketing".
commonErrors.correction_en: I work in digital marketing.

teacher.goal_pt: Networking vocabulary: to break the ice, common ground, to touch base, to stay in touch, a lead, to put someone in touch with.
prompts: How do you usually break the ice?
Can you put me in touch with someone in your company?
watchFor: "Contact" used with "with" ("contact with me"); the verb takes a direct object.
"Stay in contact" is fine, but "stay in touch" is more natural.

exercises.example_en: A good question is the easiest way to break the ice.
We found some common ground: we'd both lived in Lisbon.

exercises.word_en: to put someone in touch with
exercises.example_en: I can put you in touch with our head of sales.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each networking expression with its meaning.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Seria ótimo manter contato."

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Manter contato" is "stay in touch" or "keep in touch". "Maintain contact" sounds bureaucratic.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Seria" is conditional: "It would be great", not "It will be great".
commonErrors.correction_en: It'd be great to stay in touch.

teacher.goal_pt: Sound engaged: rising intonation on genuine questions, stress on key information in your pitch.
prompts: Ask "Oh really? How did you get into that?" with genuine interest.
Say your job title and company clearly.
watchFor: Mumbling the company name, the most important information.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with genuine interest in your voice.
exercises.prompt: Oh, really? How did you get into that?

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat, stressing the key words: HELP, SMALL, GROW, ONLINE.
exercises.prompt: Basically, I help small businesses grow online.
accepted: Basically, I help small businesses grow online
Basically I help small businesses to grow online

exercises.instruction_pt: How should "So, what do you do?" usually sound at a networking event?
options: Falling and friendly, as an open question.
Very high and rising, as if surprised.
Flat and fast, as a formality.
exercises.explanation_pt: "Wh-" questions usually fall in English. A warm falling tone sounds natural and interested.

teacher.goal_pt: Keep a networking conversation going: show interest, find common ground, ask follow-up questions.
prompts: What do you have in common with this person?
watchFor: Answering and then going silent instead of asking back.
Making the conversation an interview with only questions.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. What is the speaker offering?
exercises.listen: If you're interested in the fintech side, I could introduce you to my old manager. She's always on the lookout for new talent.
options: To give the listener a job.
To put the listener in touch with a useful contact.
To ask the listener for a job.
exercises.explanation_pt: "I could introduce you to..." means putting someone in touch with a contact.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and respond with interest, then ask a follow-up question.
exercises.listen: I've just moved to São Paulo from London to set up our new office.
accepted: Oh, interesting! How are you finding it so far?
That's exciting! How are you finding São Paulo?
Really? How are you settling in?
Wow, big move! How's it going so far?
Oh, nice! What made you choose São Paulo?
That's a big change! How are you finding the city?
Interesting! How are you settling in?
How are you finding it so far?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Está gostando?" is better as "How are you finding it?" or "Do you like it?". "Are you liking" is informal and avoided by many speakers.
commonErrors.correction_en: How are you finding it so far?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Se adaptando" in this context is more naturally "settling in".
commonErrors.correction_en: How are you settling in?

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. The person has to leave. Close the conversation and suggest staying in touch.

accepted: No worries! It was great talking to you. Let's stay in touch
Of course! Lovely to meet you. Shall we connect on LinkedIn?
No problem. It was great to meet you. Let's keep in touch
Sure, it was nice talking to you. Let's stay in touch
No worries. Can I get your card before you go?
Of course. Great meeting you. I'll send you a message
No problem! Let's stay in touch
It was great meeting you. Let's keep in touch
It was nice to meet you. Let's stay in touch
Nice meeting you. Let's keep in touch

commonErrors.match: ^(no problem |no worries |sure |of course )?nice to meet you\b
commonErrors.explanation_pt: At the end of a conversation, use the -ing or past form: "Nice meeting you" / "It was nice to meet you". "Nice to meet you" is for the start.
commonErrors.correction_en: It was great meeting you. Let's stay in touch.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Say "stay in touch" or "keep in touch".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was great meeting you. Let's stay in touch.

teacher.goal_pt: Role-play a full networking exchange: open, pitch, common ground, close and follow up.
prompts: I'm standing alone by the coffee. Come and talk to me.
It's been great chatting. What's the best way to reach you?
watchFor: "Work with" for a field; "I am engineer" without an article.
